title: Rabbi Chanina ben Gamla
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Sanhedrin 111a, expounding the verse “And Moses hastened and bowed,” etc.: “What did he see? Rabbi Chanina ben Gamla said: He saw ‘long-suffering.’” Some read there ben Gamliel. In Tosefta Parah 4:8: “Rabbi Shimon said: I found Chanina ben Gamliel in Sidon”; the Gra reads Chanina ben Gamla. Hyman endorses this because Rabbi Shimon would not call Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel “Chanina,” since Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel was older than Rabbi Shimon. Hyman suggests that possibly his father’s name was Gamliel, and they called him Gamla to distinguish him from Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel the Patriarch.

notes.text: Saved Davidson Sanhedrin 111a has Chanina ben Gamla. Hyman endorses the Gra’s Gamla reading and argues that Chanina ben Gamliel was older than Rabbi Shimon, so the latter would not address him simply as Chanina. The proposed shared father-name and distinguishing nickname remain conjectural; no genealogy merge is performed.

The consulted Sanhedrin 111a names Chanina ben Gamla. The consulted Machon-Mamre Tosefta Parah 4:5 names Chanina ben Gamliel; its 4:8 concerns vessels instead of this meeting. Hyman’s supplied 4:8, Sidon report and exact Gra reading remain distinct from the consulted numbering and wording, and his age/name argument remains his.
